requirement:
In authored book chapters, a passage opted into citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary` displays its
body as ordinary Markdown prose, with the same left alignment as the
surrounding prose and no opening citation badge or enclosing border.

A small marker in the right gutter identifies the passage's citation-checking
annotations. It does not claim that recorded evidence is current or accepted.
The outermost eligible citation fence has one marker; nested commentary
belongs to its list rather than displaying another marker.

Activating the marker opens the list of resolved citations from the source
passage, including its opening citation, citation-only metadata paragraphs,
and citations within nested commentary. Citations belonging to nested
requirement or example declarations are excluded. Repeated citations appear
once. Project citations link to their declarations; built-in citations retain
their descriptive hover text. The marker is keyboard operable, has an
accessible label, and shows visible keyboard focus. Opening the list does not
hide the passage. Inline citations within explanatory prose retain their
usual rendering.

Rendering does not change the source passage, its discovered references, or
its review inputs. Unfenced citations, citations inside requirement or example
declarations, and utility-only commentary retain their existing rendering.

structural: Every clause of `requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary.display` states observable rendering or behavior. None prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field or named interface. I found no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. I checked each candidate clause against a behavior-preserving alternative: - **Prose display:** "ordinary Markdown prose, with the same left alignment ... and no opening citation badge or enclosing border". Any markup or CSS that renders this way satisfies it. `md/habeas.css#rule[.habeas-citation-passage]` sets `border: 0` and `padding: 0`, but that is one way to get the look. - **Right-gutter marker:** "A small marker in the right gutter". Absolute positioning, a float or a grid column would all produce the same result. `md/habeas.css#rule[.habeas-citation-list]` uses absolute positioning with a negative `right`. - **Single marker and de-duplicated list:** "one marker", "nested commentary belongs to its list", "Repeated citations appear once", "Project citations link to their declarations". These describe what the output contains. The rendering code that builds the HTML could be organized in many ways. - **Keyboard operation:** "keyboard operable, has an accessible label, and shows visible keyboard focus". A `details`/`summary` element, a button or a custom widget would all work. `md/habeas.css#rule[.habeas-citation-list%20>%20summary:focus-visible]` draws an outline, which is one way to show focus. - **Opening the list:** "Opening the list does not hide the passage". This is behavior. - **No change to source:** "Rendering does not change the source passage, its discovered references, or its review inputs". This is a behavioral constraint. The supplied root `md/habeas.css` is the stylesheet, so it only supplies presentation for these behaviors. The rules I read, `rule[.habeas-citation-passage]`, `rule[.habeas-citation-list]`, `rule[.habeas-citation-list > summary]` and its `:focus-visible` rule, are consistent with the display behavior. They are not prescribed structure. behavioral: I found no test-adequacy gap. Two tests in `src/lib.rs` cover the obligations: `mod[tests]/fn[reviewed_passages_show_one_gutter_list_and_preserve_prose_and_literal_contexts]` and `mod[tests]/fn[citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details]`. I did not request implementation source. **Prose display, no badge or border, left alignment** - The first test splits the output at ` `. It asserts that the nested prose, nested requirement and example text, and the ordinary paragraph all remain in the output after the gutter details block. It also checks that the pulldown-cmark HTML renders `

`, so the body is ordinary Markdown. - It asserts that the nested `::::{cite} rules.ready` opening fence line is gone from the prose. - It asserts that the CSS for `.habeas-citation-passage` has `padding: 0`, `border: 0` and a left margin of `0`. This covers "no enclosing border" and "same left alignment". - The second test covers the absence of an opening badge in the prose. For `:::{cite} rules.ready`, the `alt="cite rules.ready"` badge appears exactly once, in the annotations before the prose. The other cite, `rules.other`, and `habeas:util` do not appear in the visible prose. **One right-gutter marker, none for nested commentary** - The test asserts exactly one `habeas-citation-passage` and one `habeas-citation-list`, even though the source has a nested `::::{cite}` fence inside the outer one. - The CSS assertions check `position: relative` on the passage, `position: absolute` on the marker, and `right:` without `left:`. - The marker is a `※` summary titled "Show citations". ::::{req} citation_review.book_commentary
A closed `:::{cite} full.name` fence in the book, outside a requirement or
example declaration, opts its explanatory passage into citation review.
A passage needs a review when it contains at least one resolved citation
other than `habeas:util`.
The outermost eligible citation fence identifies the passage. Its opening
citation and citations throughout its body belong to one review, including
citations inside nested commentary containers. References inside nested
requirement or example declarations belong to those declarations' assessments.
The review's subject is the enclosing citation fence's outline node, rather
than the whole chapter. Its inputs include the passage and each cited
declaration or built-in text, with the terminology they use. For project
requirements and examples, the reviewer checks that the passage's claims agree
with and are supported by the cited declarations. Contradicting or unsupported
claims produce a negative assessment. Built-in citations retain their
permitted-role and stated-criteria checks under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
These passages use the citation-review storage, freshness checks, selection,
and `author --all` workflow of {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
Their identities follow the existing outline-selector rules. Rendering follows
{cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`. Unfenced book citations retain
their existing behavior.
